_comment: The current targeting snapshot, loaded by `manage.py targeting_import --from-manifest`. Rebuilding this dataset from source costs 30-45 minutes of API calls and can exhaust WorldPop's daily quota for everyone else, so a new environment should restore from here rather than re-fetch. Pin a new drive_file_id whenever the dataset changes materially: export, upload to the folder below (shared with connect-labs-sa), and update the id, created_at and counts in one commit so the file and the record stay together.
notes:
Restore with: make manage CMD="targeting_import --from-manifest --prune" (needs LABS_SYNTHETIC_GDRIVE_SA_KEY; already in the ECS task definition, and locally readable from Secrets Manager as labs-jj-synthetic-gdrive-sa-key with the labs AWS profile). USE --prune. This snapshot is the first that is authoritative rather than additive, and it has to be: 13,054 derived rows carrying a PREVIOUS VERSION OF THE ARITHMETIC were swept out of the source database, and an un-pruned restore would leave every one of them on the target, indistinguishable from the corrected values. See derive.sweep_derived. 

122,885 values against 105,069 on 1 September. What changed: fever_prevalence was loaded for the first time (466 rows, 38 countries) -- it had been in the registry and in the child_health stage and had never actually run, which is why malaria_treatment_gap could not derive under the conditional_on rule and kept 1,700 rows of the six-times-too-high pre-fix shape. Every conditional coverage measure now also carries a *_gap_annual sibling, the fortnight figure carried to a year at 365/(recall + episode duration); for diarrhoea that is x19.9, which turns Liberia's 15.7% two-week prevalence into 3.13 episodes per child-year, inside the 2.7-3.3 range Fischer Walker et al. report for sub-Saharan Africa. Both counts are kept side by side because quoting the fortnight one as a year's is a twentyfold error this system has made in print. 

Every surviving derived row sits at ADM0/1/2 on a geoBoundaries boundary this app owns. Liberia's ORS figures are unchanged to the digit (713,882 under-fives, 51,429 untreated in a fortnight, 1,025,769 a year; 791,563 / 60,671 / 1,210,108 projected to 2027). Research notes are NOT in this snapshot -- they live in git and are written by `manage.py seed_targeting_research`, which should be run after any import.
